newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat calls U.S. envoy's talks "fruitful".
newsitem.headline: Arafat calls U.S. envoy's talks "fruitful".

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat said talks on Sunday with U.S. peace broker Dennis Ross were "constructive and fruitful" and they both hoped to give a boost to Israel-PLO negotiations stuck on a Hebron accord.

"It was very constructive and fruitful and an important meeting. We discussed how to push the peace process forward in all means," Arafat told reporters after a 2-1/2-hour meeting that began on Sunday after midnight.

Israelis and Palestinians accuse each other of foot-dragging in talks on Hebron. Arafat has demanded Israel implement the partial withdrawal agreement it signed more than a year ago. Netanyahu has sought changes to protect some 400 militant Jewish settlers in the heart of the West Bank town of 100,000 Arabs.

Ross, on a mission for President Bill Clinton and Secretary of State Warren Christopher, travelled to the self-ruled Gaza Strip late on Saturday hours after arriving in Israel and meeting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Jerusalem.

"The president and the secretary have sent me out here because they wanted me to see what could be done to energise the process and also to have the chance to meet the leaders," Ross said, adding that he would report back to the president and they would decide how to proceed.

Palestinians were encouraged when Clinton criticised Israel's expansion of Jewish settlements in the West Bank last week but Christopher's comments on Thursday that Palestinians had to make concessions on Hebron irked PLO leaders.
